sentences.text: Perusal of the record would reveal that the detenu and his wife i.e., the writ petitioner herein were arrested in TADA Case by the Police of Sanathnagar Police Station in the year 1993.

The Police have seized his Auto-rickshaw, Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Only) cash given by Shakamuri Appa Rao, an active Member of the banned PWG, who involved in K.S. Vyas, IPS (former DIG of Police)
Murder Case.
The Police have also seized grenade empty cups.
Prisoner on Transit (PT) warrants were issued against the detenu and his wife.

The same were executed and he was sent to Musheerabad Jail, where he came into contact with notorious Gangster, Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and his associate, who was also in Jail in K.S. Vyas, IPS murder case.
According to the respondent authorities, the detenu continued his connections with Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and involved in nine (09) murder cases and extortion cases.
After the death of Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem in the year 2016, he went into anonymity for some period.
Thereafter, he started dealing with Real Estate Brokers to create his own image in the Society.
In the said process, he developed friendship with Mohd. Abdullah @ Suresh Goud and other realtors for settlement of disputes by showing the weapons (firearms).
He possessed one country made pistol KL,J & PSS,J chambering 7.65 mm caliber semi rimmed metallic cartridges which was fired previously.
It is in working condition.
The aforesaid cartridge is company made and is live.

The detenu with his illegal acts created terror, panic and fear in the minds of the general public by using prohibited firearm and thereby committed the aforesaid offences and disturbed public order and also tranquility in the area.
Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which would disturb the public order, respondent No.2 issued the impugned detention order dated 25.12.2022.

The same was approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2457, dated 31.12.2022 and confirmed vide G.O.Rt.No.321, dated 28.02.2023.
7.

Mr. Basa Chanakya, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the aforesaid eleven (11) crimes were referred, the same were not relied on by respondent No.2, the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order.
The aforesaid two (02) crimes have to be read in isolation.
Therefore, the aforesaid 11 cases are stale cases and the same cannot be considered for the purpose of issuance of detention order.

In the aforesaid two (02) crimes relied upon by respondent No.2, the detaining authority while issuing detention order, he has not considered the fact that the allegation KL,J & PSS,J against the detenu is that he has possessed firearms illegally,
but he has not used the said firearms in any crime.
i) He would further submit that the detenu has not committed any incident/act, such as murder etc.
Even then, respondent No.2 invoked his powers under Act No.1 of 1986 and issued the impugned detention order.
The detenu did not attempt by using the alleged firearms and he has not brandished any offence.
Even as per the counter and the impugned detention order, the detenu did not commit any offence after 2016.
Even then, respondent No.2 issued impugned detention order illegally.
There was no material before respondent No.2 to come to subjective satisfaction with regard to the disturbance caused to the public order due to the alleged acts committed by the detenu.

sentences.text: The bail applications filed by the detenu were dismissed.
Even in other crimes, PT warrants were issued against the detenu and the police have executed the same.
Thus, the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature.
He and his wife, the writ petitioner herein, were Members of PWG.
PT warrants were executed against them.
The police have produced them before the concerned Courts.
They were in Jail in 1993 itself.
They were arrested under TADA.

Thereafter, during his judicial custody in Musheerabad Jail, he got acquaintance with notorious Gangster, Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem and his associates and he has committed several offences including murders of the people mentioned in the aforesaid crimes.
After the death of Nayeemuddin KL,J & PSS,J @ Nayeem in the year 2016, he was silent for some period and, thereafter, he started involving in real-estate disputes.
The aforesaid two (02) crimes were registered in the year 2022 on the ground of detenu possessing firearms illegally.

The bail applications filed by the detenu in the old case were dismissed and in the aforesaid two crimes,
though bails were granted, he could not furnish sureties and, therefore, he is continuing in judicial custody.
Thus, according to the respondents, the case of the detenu falls under the category of 'Arms Offender'.

13. It is relevant to note that Section - 2 (u) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "Arms Offender",
which means a person who commits or abets the commission of offences punishable under Act No.1 of 1986.
14. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration5 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.

The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.
.
(1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & PSS,J 15

. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar6, the Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District Magistrate is entitled to take action .
(1966) 1 SCR 709 KL,J & PSS,J under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

It will thus appear Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/
5

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
16.

In Mallada K. Sri Ram1, the Apex Court considering the fact that only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu and he was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, set aside the detention order.

17. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar7, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean . AIR 1984 SC 1334 KL,J & PSS,J 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'.

entities.text: Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.

18. Thus, the detaining authority while invoking the powers under the Act No.1 of 1986, has to consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction that due to the acts committed by the detenu, nature of offences and the manner in which the same were committed would disturb the public order.
To prevent the detenu from committing the similar offences, the detaining authority shall issue preventive detention order against the detenu.
19. There is no dispute with regard to the legal proposition that the detention order shall be issued in rarest of rare cases, that too, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.

Article - 21 of the Constitution of India enshrined the detenu the fundamental right of personal liberty which is precious right enshrined to the citizens as per KL,J & PSS,J the Constitution of India.
At the same time, duty cast upon the 'State' as defined under Article - 12 of the Constitution of India to maintain law and order as well as public order.
When there is disturbance to the public order, it is the duty of the 'State' to invoke the procedure laid down under the Act No.1 of 1986, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
20. In Vijay Kumar3, the detention order was passed when the detenu was in Jail.

Considering the said facts, the Apex Court held that though the detenu is in Jail, the impugned detention order can be passed relying on the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the nature of offences and manner in which it was committed.
21. In Smt. K. Aruna Kumari4, the Apex Court held that this Court cannot examine probative value of evidence available to the detaining authority.

sentences.text: As discussed above, the facts of the present case would reveal that the detenu is having criminal history and several cases are pending against him.
In all the aforesaid cases, the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature.
He has used firearms in the aforesaid crimes and committed murder of several people.
He KL,J & PSS,J and his wife were Members of banned PWG and TADA was invoked against them.
He has closely associated with notorious Gangster, namely Nayeemuddin @ Nayeem, and after his death, he has involved in the aforesaid two (02) crimes.

Therefore, the facts of the present case are different to the facts of the case in Mallada K. Sri Ram1,
wherein only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections - 420, 468, 471 and 506 read with 120B of IPC and, therefore, the Apex Court considering the same and that the detenu was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, set aside the detention order.
23. In Smt. T. Usha Bhai2, the detaining authority invoked the preventive detention order against the husband of the petitioner, a sitting MLA on the allegation of giving hate speeches.
Therefore, the facts of the said case are different to the facts of the present case.
24. As rightly contended by learned Special Government Pleader that the detenu is possessing firearms illegally and there is every possibility of the detenu using the same in committing the offences.
Earlier he has committed the aforesaid offences which are serious in nature.
Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing KL,J & PSS,J similar offences, respondent No.2 has passed the impugned detention order.
In view of the same, the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the detenu did not use the firearms and he has not brandished the same in commission of offence is unsustainable.
25. As discussed above, in the present case, the allegations levelled against the detenu are very serious.

Therefore, viewed from any angle, according to this Court, there is no error in the impugned detention order passed by respondent No.2 and approved and confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt. Nos.2457 and 321, dated 31.12.2022 and 28.02.2023 respectively.
Thus, the writ petition fails and the same is liable to be dismissed.
26. The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
In the circumstances of the cases, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.

Smt. Muddunuri Narsamma vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40168320/
6 22.
Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing KL,J & PSS,J similar offences, respondent No.2 has passed the impugned detention order.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, viewed from any angle, according to this Court, there is no error in the impugned detention order passed by respondent No.2 and approved and confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt. Nos.2457 and 321, dated 31.12.2022 and 28.02.2023 respectively.
Thus, the writ petition fails and the same is liable to be dismissed.
26. The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
In the circumstances of the cases, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.
